query: If airlines eliminated the most common cabin-service complaints in the reviews, how much would the average Overall Rating improve?

per_column.name: is_food_service_complaint
per_column.rationale: This binary flag isolates food/cabin-service complaints, which is exactly the grouping axis the query needs to identify the 'complaint' subset, so it carries genuine analytical leverage (not near-constant: ~2346/8100 flagged). Groundedness is weak, however: sample 3 ('Food was plentiful and tasty' / 'Excellent performance on all fronts') is a clearly POSITIVE food mention yet is flagged 1, i.e. the classifier confuses 'food is mentioned' with 'food is complained about'. Samples 1, 2, 4, 5 are handled correctly, but the sentiment-confusion error is a substantive false positive that undermines trust in the flag.

per_column.name: predicted_overall_rating
per_column.rationale: As a modeled baseline it is largely redundant with the existing original 'Overall Rating' column, so on its own it adds limited new leverage; its main value is as the reference point for the counterfactual lift. Directionally the predictions are mostly reasonable (glowing reviews ~9.5, 'dreadful seats' ~1.63), but sample 1 explicitly states 'overall this flight is a 9/10' while the model predicts 7.38, a notable deviation from a source that gives an explicit score. Values are model estimates rather than invented facts, so no outright hallucination, but grounding is only moderate.

per_column.name: predicted_overall_rating_no_food_complaint
per_column.rationale: This is the counterfactual 'complaint removed' rating that the query directly asks about, so it is analytically on-point and gives a real comparison axis against the baseline prediction. Grounding is only moderate: for non-flagged rows it correctly equals the baseline, but the counterfactual uplift is an opaque model output and inherits errors from the flawed complaint flag (e.g. sample 3 gets an uplift 8.98->9.08 despite the underlying review being positive, so the counterfactual is applied where no complaint actually exists).

per_column.name: food_complaint_rating_lift
per_column.rationale: This is essentially the metric the query wants (per-review rating improvement from eliminating the food complaint), so it is directly relevant. It is docked because it is a mechanical difference of the two prediction columns (a restatement) and is near-constant within the complaint group (~0.1-0.14), reflecting a crude fixed-bump model rather than a rich per-row estimate. Values are internally consistent with the two prediction columns but again depend on the accuracy of the complaint flag.

judge.rationale: The added columns form a coherent, purpose-built pipeline for the query: flag food/cabin-service complaints, predict a baseline rating, predict a no-complaint counterfactual, and expose the per-row lift. This directly supports estimating how average Overall Rating would change if complaints were removed, so table-level usefulness is solid, though somewhat diluted by the baseline prediction being redundant with the existing Overall Rating column and the lift being a mechanical restatement of the two prediction columns. Groundedness is the weaker dimension: the core complaint flag exhibits a sentiment-confusion false positive (positive food praise flagged as a complaint in sample 3), one baseline prediction contradicts an explicit in-text 9/10 score, and the counterfactual/lift values are opaque, near-constant model outputs that inherit the flag's errors. Silent-row behaviour and correctly-flagged rows are handled well, but the observed errors keep grounding at a moderate level.
